q7.answer: The refresh loop builds a new immutable SecretCache snapshot and swaps its reference, which happens every 5 minutes plus up to 30 seconds of jitter. Each provider HTTP call reads the current snapshot when it is made and puts that key in the Authorization header, so the next call uses the new key, while a request already in flight keeps the key it read and finishes with it.

q8.answer: Step 5 confirms it in two ways. First, each of the 4 prod pods must report the store's latest version id for all three secrets, checked through the secret_version metric or the version-change log lines, after at least one full 5-minute refresh cycle plus a margin. Second, each old key must show zero last-used activity at its provider for a window Security sets (suggested 30 minutes) that starts when the last old pod stops. Where the metric is viewed is still open (Open question 8).

q9.answer: The order is: Step 0 checks provider capabilities (overlap, disable, last-used visibility); Step 1 sets store namespaces, KMS keys and access policy; Step 2 issues new provider keys and writes them to orders-api/prod/* as v1 while old keys stay live; Step 3 merges the code change and removes the api_key values from config/app.yaml in the same PR, then verifies it in dev; Step 4 rolls out to prod with the write freeze; Step 5 confirms every instance is on the new version; Step 6 disables the old keys at the providers; Step 7 deletes them after the soak. Step 8 (migration marker) must be in place before Step 6, and Step 9 (CI guard) ships with the Step 3 PR.

q10.answer: make run sets APP_ENV=dev and reads orders-api/dev/* with the developer's own dev-only role, so developers never read prod secrets and the local run uses sandbox keys rather than live ones. The guard refuses to start if the identity is orders-api-prod while APP_ENV is dev. Who creates the dev sandbox keys and writes them to orders-api/dev/* is not decided and is listed as Open question 9.

q11.answer: The attempt fails if any one of the three secrets is missing, and a failed attempt keeps nothing, so the gate retries the full fetch of all three (up to 3 retries, 2 seconds apart; whether that means 3 retries or 3 total attempts is still open, Open question 3). If every attempt fails, the app logs the secret names and error classes, never values, and exits non-zero, so Kubernetes restarts it with crash-loop backoff while /healthz stays 503 and the rollout halts with the old pods still serving.
